column3: After the uproar ceased, Paul sent for the disciples and encouraged them, and after saying farewell, he departed to go to Macedonia.
And after passing through those regions and encouraging them with many words, he came to Greece.
After spending three months there, when a plot was made against him by the Jews as he was about to sail to Syria, he decided to return through Macedonia.
And Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea accompanied him, and from the Thessalonians Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius from Derbe and Timothy, and from Asia Tychicus and Trophimus.
These went on ahead and were waiting for us in Troas.
But we sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread and came to them in Troas within five days, where we stayed seven days.
Now on the first day of the week, when we were gathered to break bread, Paul began speaking to them, intending to depart the next day, and he extended his message until midnight.
There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we were gathered.

And a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul kept speaking for a long time. Overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was picked up dead.
But Paul went down, fell upon him, embraced him, and said, “Do not be troubled, for his life is in him.”
Then going back up and breaking the bread and eating, he talked for a considerable time until dawn, and so he departed.
And they brought the boy away alive and were comforted beyond measure.
But we went ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, intending to take Paul aboard from there, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go by land.
And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.
And sailing from there, on the following day we arrived opposite Chios, and the next day we crossed over to Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so that he would not spend time in Asia, because he was hurrying, if possible, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
But from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and summoned the elders of the assembly.
And when they came to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know from the first day on which I entered Asia how I was with you the whole time,
serving the Lord with all humility and with tears and trials that happened to me through the plots of the Jews,
how I held back nothing of what was beneficial from declaring it to you and teaching you publicly and from house to house,
solemnly testifying both to Jews and Greeks repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
And now, look, bound in the spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there,
except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that chains and afflictions await me.
But I consider my life worth nothing to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to solemnly testify to the good news of the grace of God.
And now, look, I know that none of you among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom will see my face again.
Therefore I testify to you on this very day that I am clean from the blood of all,
for I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole purpose of God.
Pay attention to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit appointed you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of God, which he acquired through his own blood.
I know that after my departure fierce wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock,
and from among your own selves men will arise speaking twisted things to draw away the disciples after them.
Therefore stay awake, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not stop admonishing each one with tears.
And now I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
I coveted no one’s silver or gold or clothing.
You yourselves know that these hands served my needs and those who were with me.
In everything I showed you that by working hard in this way we must help the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
And after saying these things, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
Then there was much weeping among them all, and falling on Paul’s neck, they were kissing him,
being especially grieved over the word he had spoken, that they were about to see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.
